title: The WORST Bodybuilding Program Ever Created (my bad)
summary: NH roasts BBBS, the seven-day powerbuilding program he wrote in 2017 and planned to sell for $40. It gave him his worst plateau (2017-2019), along with knee, shoulder and SI-joint problems. He goes through every day, explains what he does instead now, and shows that both his physique and his strength improved once he dropped the big-three and 1RM obsession for hypertrophy-oriented exercise selection.
claims: Most influencer programs are gimmicky cash grabs written in minutes because people will buy them anyway
He wrote BBBS in 2017 at the peak of his powerbuilding phase, after 7 years of training of which only 2 were in a gym, and was convinced he was a programming genius
BBBS gave him the biggest plateau of his life from 2017 to 2019 with barely any muscle or strength gained, constant injuries and damaged mental health; recovery took until 2020
BBBS ran 7 days a week with no rest days, rotating bench, squat, arms and deadlift days; days built around a movement rather than muscles make it a powerlifting program, not a hypertrophy one
Working up to a 1RM and stopping there skips the hard sets that drive growth; the warm-up is all you get
Back-off sets with a huge drop are junk volume; after working sets at 275 lb, drop to around 245, not 185
Always doing overhead press for 8-12 reps made it plateau, especially when he was not gaining weight
If your bench goes up while push-ups and pull-ups go down, your bulk is adding fat rather than muscle
An upper body day should train at least three muscle groups, including arm isolation and abs
Squatting 2-3 times a week with the same stance and technique eventually causes overuse knee pain and a plateau

Front squats are not worth it for most bodybuilders: they take mobility work, are limited by thoracic extension, and gave him wrist pain that hurt his upper-body training; a hack squat does the job better
Balance squat days with a hip hinge instead of only knee-flexion or extension work
Minimalism works for legs, but BBBS was too extreme, with no neck, abs, forearms or rear delts
Cheat curls were his only biceps exercise from 15 to about 22 and they built big arms, but that is survivorship bias; most people should use other curl variations
He chose front raises because cheating let him use more weight; a bodybuilder should pick variations that work the muscle with less weight
Five years of dumbbell rows with his torso parallel to the floor gave him concrete erectors, but his lats lagged
His giant sets started on the BBBS arm days
Pin presses did not break his overhead press plateau
Cutting range of motion to lift more is ego lifting; if 10 lb dumbbells challenge you, use them
He skipped triceps isolation for 7 years believing presses were enough, and his triceps still lag; beginners should isolate every muscle from the start
Shoulders need 1-2 vertical presses plus 1-2 isolation movements, including side delts and some external rotation, upright rows or face pulls
A 3x3 deadlift is a fine scheme if you leave reps in the tank
Bodybuilders do not need deadlifts; RDLs, stiff-leg deadlifts, good mornings or hyperextensions work better, and some people are not built for conventional pulls
After pulling in the 400s he did AMRAP sets with 315, adding more fatigue for no reason
The metallic bar feeling across the pelvis on deadlift days is SI joint overuse, not a pump; he felt it every session on BBBS and no longer does with proper volume
Deadlifts, deficit pulls and Pendlay rows have no eccentric; RDLs are better because you get the stretch
Touch-and-go bench combined with his scoliosis injured his shoulder again and again, each time costing about three weeks off, for two years
Bench suits him only with a very close, paused grip; he built his chest with push-ups and now grows best on weighted incline ring push-ups and dips with three plates, pain-free
He stopped push-ups because YouTube said they were for noobs; that was wrong
Barbell overhead press stalled forever; on the Smith machine he adds 5-10 lb a month to vertical presses
A lift that does not let you progress is not a good lift for you
Pulling with your back is a skill: practice scapular retractions on a pull-up bar first, and use weighted pull-ups as the main lift with pulldowns as a complement
He now back squats about once a month and PRs pain-free each time; most quad volume comes from belt squats, heel-elevated SSB squats and split squats
Unilateral leg work is good for hypertrophy, not just for athletes
Testing a deadlift 1RM every two weeks kept him stuck between 465 and 485 lb for a year; he never pulled 495
Constant max testing is like smashing a piggy bank every two weeks; you test strength but never build it
Now he deadlifts about every 40 days, gets 95% of posterior-chain volume from RDLs, good mornings and hyperextensions, and PRs each time
Dropping PR culture made him stronger; obsessing over 1RMs kept him from training properly
Partial low-bar squats with about five plates and almost no knee bend were pure ego lifting that loaded the SI joint and did nothing for the quads
Starting a session with a 1RM wrecks the rest of the day: fatigue lowers the intensity of later work and a failed max kills motivation
Specificity is not important for bodybuilding; pick the variations that let you progress
The big three made up about 80% of BBBS and around 70% of its exercises could be replaced with better hypertrophy lifts
Being obsessed with putting weight on the bar created progression anxiety that kept him from progressing
The BBBS physique had good biceps, chest and quads, but a poorly defined back with no lat flare, nonexistent shoulders and very poor triceps
His abs were good only because of years of daily ab training before BBBS
His triceps will never fully catch up to his biceps after five years of neglect
His BBBS best lifts were a 335 lb bench single, 395 lb squat for 7 and 495 lb deadlift single at 240 lb; he now beats all but the bench at 220 lb
He planned to sell BBBS for $40; if he would market that garbage, others do too, so stop buying programs and learn to write your own
He is glad he waited to start the channel, since in 2016 he would have spread misinformation for years
